speaker: israelites
name: The Israelites
text: Who will be the first to go up and fight for us against the Canaanites?

speaker: god
name: The LORD
text: Judah shall go up,

speaker: god
text: Indeed, I have delivered the land into their hands.

speaker: men-of-judah
name: The men of Judah
text: Come up with us to our allotted territory, and let us fight against the Canaanites. And we likewise will go with you to your territory.

speaker: adoni-bezek
name: Adoni-bezek
text: Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off have gathered the scraps under my table. As I have done to them, so God has repaid me.

speaker: caleb
name: Caleb
text: To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.

speaker: caleb
text: What do you desire?

speaker: acsah
name: Acsah
text: Give me a blessing,

speaker: acsah
text: Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well.

speaker: spies-of-house-of-joseph
name: The spies of the house of Joseph
text: Please show us how to get into the city, and we will treat you kindly.

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
name: The angel of the LORD
text: I brought you up out of Egypt and led you into the land that I had promised to your fathers, and I said, ‘I will never break My covenant with you,

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: I will never break My covenant with you,

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: and you are not to make a covenant with the people of this land, but you shall tear down their altars.’ Yet you have not obeyed My voice. What is this you have done?

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: and you are not to make a covenant with the people of this land, but you shall tear down their altars.

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: So now I tell you that I will not drive out these people before you; they will be thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you.

speaker: god
name: The LORD
text: Because this nation has transgressed the covenant I laid down for their fathers and has not heeded My voice,

speaker: god
text: I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.

speaker: god
text: In this way I will test whether Israel will keep the way of the LORD by walking in it as their fathers did.

speaker: ehud
name: Ehud
text: I have a secret message for you, O king.

speaker: eglon
name: Eglon
text: Silence,

speaker: ehud
text: I have a word from God for you,

speaker: servants-of-eglon
name: Eglon’s servants
text: He must be relieving himself in the cool room,

speaker: ehud
text: Follow me,

speaker: ehud
text: for the LORD has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.

speaker: deborah
name: Deborah
text: Surely the LORD, the God of Israel, is commanding you: ‘Go and march to Mount Tabor, taking with you ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun.

speaker: god
name: The LORD
text: Go and march to Mount Tabor, taking with you ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun.
tag: the LORD, the God of Israel

speaker: deborah
text: And I will draw out Sisera the commander of Jabin’s army, his chariots, and his troops to the River Kishon, and I will deliver him into your hand.’

speaker: god
text: And I will draw out Sisera the commander of Jabin’s army, his chariots, and his troops to the River Kishon, and I will deliver him into your hand.

speaker: barak
name: Barak
text: If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.

speaker: deborah
text: I will certainly go with you,

speaker: deborah
text: but the road you are taking will bring you no honor, because the LORD will be selling Sisera into the hand of a woman.

speaker: deborah
text: Arise, for this is the day that the LORD has delivered Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone before you?

speaker: jael
name: Jael
text: Come in, my lord. Come in with me. Do not be afraid.

speaker: sisera
name: Sisera
text: Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.

speaker: sisera
text: Stand at the entrance to the tent,

speaker: sisera
text: and if anyone comes and asks you, ‘Is there a man here?’ say, ‘No.’

speaker: unnamed-inquirer
name: Unnamed inquirer
text: Is there a man here?

speaker: jael
text: No.

speaker: jael
text: Come, and I will show you the man you are seeking.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
name: Deborah and Barak
text: When the princes take the lead in Israel, when the people volunteer, bless the LORD.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Listen, O kings! Give ear, O princes! I will sing to the LORD; I will sing praise to the LORD, the God of Israel.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: O LORD, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from the land of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens poured out rain, and the clouds poured down water.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: The mountains quaked before the LORD, the One of Sinai, before the LORD, the God of Israel.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted and the travelers took the byways.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Life in the villages ceased; it ended in Israel, until I, Deborah, arose, a mother in Israel.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: When they chose new gods, then war came to their gates. Not a shield or spear was found among forty thousand in Israel.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: My heart is with the princes of Israel, with the volunteers among the people. Bless the LORD!

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: You who ride white donkeys, who sit on saddle blankets, and you who travel the road, ponder

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: the voices of the singers at the watering places. There they shall recount the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous deeds of His villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates:

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: ‘Awake, awake, O Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, O Barak, and take hold of your captives, O son of Abinoam!’

speaker: israelites
name: The Israelites
text: Awake, awake, O Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, O Barak, and take hold of your captives, O son of Abinoam!

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the people of the LORD came down to me against the mighty.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Some came from Ephraim, with their roots in Amalek; Benjamin came with your people after you. The commanders came down from Machir, the bearers of the marshal’s staff from Zebulun.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah, and Issachar was with Barak, rushing into the valley at his heels. In the clans of Reuben there was great indecision.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Why did you sit among the sheepfolds to hear the whistling for the flocks? In the clans of Reuben there was great indecision.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Gilead remained beyond the Jordan. Dan, why did you linger by the ships? Asher stayed at the coast and remained in his harbors.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Zebulun was a people who risked their lives; Naphtali, too, on the heights of the battlefield.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, but they took no plunder of silver.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: From the heavens the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: The River Kishon swept them away, the ancient river, the River Kishon. March on, O my soul, in strength!

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Then the hooves of horses thundered— the mad galloping of his stallions.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: ‘Curse Meroz,’ says the angel of the LORD. ‘Bitterly curse her inhabitants; for they did not come to help the LORD, to help the LORD against the mighty.’

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
name: The angel of the LORD
text: Curse Meroz,

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: Bitterly curse her inhabitants; for they did not come to help the LORD, to help the LORD against the mighty.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, most blessed of tent-dwelling women.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: He asked for water, and she gave him milk. In a magnificent bowl she brought him curds.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: She reached for the tent peg, her right hand for the workman’s hammer. She struck Sisera and crushed his skull; she shattered and pierced his temple.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: At her feet he collapsed, he fell, there he lay still; at her feet he collapsed, he fell; where he collapsed, there he fell dead.

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Sisera’s mother looked through the window; she peered through the lattice and lamented: ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? What has delayed the clatter of his chariots?’

speaker: mother-of-sisera
name: Sisera’s mother
text: Why is his chariot so long in coming? What has delayed the clatter of his chariots?

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: Her wisest ladies answer; indeed she keeps telling herself,

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: ‘Are they not finding and dividing the spoil— a girl or two for each warrior, a plunder of dyed garments for Sisera, the spoil of embroidered garments for the neck of the looter?’

speaker: mother-of-sisera
text: Are they not finding and dividing the spoil— a girl or two for each warrior, a plunder of dyed garments for Sisera, the spoil of embroidered garments for the neck of the looter?

speaker: deborah-and-barak
text: So may all Your enemies perish, O LORD! But may those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest.

speaker: unnamed-prophet
name: Unnamed prophet
text: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I brought you up out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

speaker: god
name: The LORD
text: I brought you up out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
tag: the LORD, the God of Israel

speaker: unnamed-prophet
text: I delivered you out of the hands of Egypt and all your oppressors. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.

speaker: god
text: I delivered you out of the hands of Egypt and all your oppressors. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.

speaker: unnamed-prophet
text: And I said to you: ‘I am the LORD your God. You must not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.’ But you did not obey Me.

speaker: god
text: And I said to you: ‘I am the LORD your God. You must not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.’ But you did not obey Me.

speaker: god
text: I am the LORD your God. You must not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
name: The angel of the LORD
text: The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.

speaker: gideon
name: Gideon
text: Please, my Lord,

speaker: gideon
text: if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? And where are all His wonders of which our fathers told us, saying, ‘Has not the LORD brought us up out of Egypt?’ But now the LORD has forsaken us and delivered us into the hand of Midian.

speaker: fathers-of-israel
name: The fathers of Israel
text: Has not the LORD brought us up out of Egypt?

speaker: god
text: Go in the strength you have and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Am I not sending you?

speaker: gideon
text: Please, my Lord,

speaker: gideon
text: how can I save Israel? Indeed, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father’s house.

speaker: god
text: Surely I will be with you,

speaker: god
text: and you will strike down all the Midianites as one man.

speaker: gideon
text: If I have found favor in Your sight, give me a sign that it is You speaking with me.

speaker: gideon
text: Please do not depart from this place until I return to You. Let me bring my offering and set it before You.

speaker: god
text: I will stay until you return.

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: Take the meat and the unleavened bread, lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.

speaker: gideon
text: Oh no, Lord GOD! I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!

speaker: god
text: Peace be with you. Do not be afraid, for you will not die.

speaker: god
text: Take your father’s young bull and a second bull seven years old, tear down your father’s altar to Baal, and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.

speaker: god
text: Then build a proper altar to the LORD your God on the top of this stronghold. And with the wood of the Asherah pole you cut down, take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering.

speaker: men-of-ophrah
name: The men of Ophrah
text: Who did this?

speaker: unnamed-informants
name: Unnamed informants
text: Gideon son of Joash did it.

speaker: men-of-ophrah
text: Bring out your son. He must die, because he has torn down Baal’s altar and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.

speaker: joash
name: Joash
text: Are you contending for Baal? Are you trying to save him? Whoever pleads his case will be put to death by morning! If Baal is a god, let him contend for himself with the one who has torn down his altar.

speaker: men-of-ophrah
text: Let Baal contend with him,

speaker: gideon
text: If You are going to save Israel by my hand, as You have said,

speaker: gideon
text: then behold, I will place a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew only on the fleece and all the ground is dry, then I will know that You are going to save Israel by my hand, as You have said.

speaker: gideon
text: Do not be angry with me; let me speak one more time. Please allow me one more test with the fleece. This time let it be dry, and the ground covered with dew.

speaker: god
name: The LORD
text: You have too many people for Me to deliver Midian into their hands, lest Israel glorify themselves over Me, saying, ‘My own hand has saved me.’

speaker: israelites
name: The Israelites
text: My own hand has saved me.

speaker: god
text: Now, therefore, proclaim in the hearing of the people: ‘Whoever is fearful and trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead.’

speaker: gideon
name: Gideon
text: Whoever is fearful and trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead.

speaker: god
text: There are still too many people. Take them down to the water, and I will sift them for you there. If I say to you, ‘This one shall go with you,’ he shall go. But if I say, ‘This one shall not go with you,’ he shall not go.

speaker: god
text: This one shall go with you,

speaker: god
text: This one shall not go with you,

speaker: god
text: Separate those who lap the water with their tongues like a dog from those who kneel to drink.

speaker: god
text: With the three hundred men who lapped the water I will save you and deliver the Midianites into your hand. But all the others are to go home.

speaker: god
text: Get up and go down against the camp, for I have delivered it into your hand.

speaker: god
text: But if you are afraid to do so, then go down to the camp with your servant Purah

speaker: god
text: and listen to what they are saying. Then your hands will be strengthened to attack the camp.

speaker: unnamed-midianite-dreamer
name: Unnamed Midianite dreamer
text: Behold, I had a dream,

speaker: unnamed-midianite-dreamer
text: and I saw a loaf of barley bread come tumbling into the Midianite camp. It struck the tent so hard that the tent overturned and collapsed.

speaker: unnamed-midianite-friend
name: Unnamed Midianite friend
text: This is nothing less than the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God has delivered Midian and the whole camp into his hand.

speaker: gideon
text: Get up, for the LORD has delivered the camp of Midian into your hand.

speaker: gideon
text: Watch me and do as I do,

speaker: gideon
text: When I come to the outskirts of the camp, do exactly as I do.

speaker: gideon
text: When I and all who are with me blow our horns, then you are also to blow your horns from all around the camp and shout, ‘For the LORD and for Gideon!’

speaker: three-hundred-men
name: The three hundred men
text: For the LORD and for Gideon!

speaker: three-hundred-men
text: A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!

speaker: gideon
text: Come down against the Midianites and seize the waters of the Jordan ahead of them as far as Beth-barah.

speaker: ephraimites
name: The men of Ephraim
text: Why have you done this to us? Why did you fail to call us when you went to fight against Midian?

speaker: gideon
name: Gideon
text: Now what have I accomplished compared to you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?

speaker: gideon
text: God has delivered Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian, into your hand. What was I able to do compared to you?

speaker: gideon
text: Please give my troops some bread, for they are exhausted, and I am still pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.

speaker: leaders-of-succoth
name: The leaders of Succoth
text: Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your army?

speaker: gideon
text: Very well,

speaker: gideon
text: when the LORD has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness!

speaker: gideon
text: When I return in triumph, I will tear down this tower!

speaker: gideon
text: Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your weary men?’

speaker: men-of-succoth
name: The men of Succoth
text: Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your weary men?

speaker: gideon
text: What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?

speaker: zebah-and-zalmunna
name: Zebah and Zalmunna
text: Men like you,

speaker: zebah-and-zalmunna
text: each one resembling the son of a king.

speaker: gideon
text: They were my brothers,

speaker: gideon
text: the sons of my mother! As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.

speaker: gideon
text: Get up and kill them.

speaker: zebah-and-zalmunna
text: Get up and kill us yourself, for as the man is, so is his strength.

speaker: israelites
name: The Israelites
text: Rule over us—you and your son and grandson—for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.

speaker: gideon
text: I will not rule over you, nor will my son. The LORD shall rule over you.

speaker: gideon
text: Let me make a request of you, that each of you give me an earring from his plunder.

speaker: israelites
text: We will give them gladly,

speaker: abimelech
name: Abimelech
text: Please ask all the leaders of Shechem, ‘Is it better for you that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or just one man?’ Remember that I am your own flesh and blood.

speaker: relatives-of-abimelech
name: Abimelech’s mother’s brothers and clan
text: Is it better for you that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or just one man?

speaker: leaders-of-shechem
name: The leaders of Shechem
text: He is our brother.

speaker: jotham
name: Jotham
text: Listen to me, O leaders of Shechem, and may God listen to you.

speaker: jotham
text: One day the trees set out to anoint a king for themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’

speaker: trees
name: The trees
text: Reign over us.

speaker: jotham
text: But the olive tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my oil that honors both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’

speaker: olive-tree
name: The olive tree
text: Should I stop giving my oil that honors both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?

speaker: jotham
text: Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’

speaker: trees
text: Come and reign over us.

speaker: jotham
text: But the fig tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my sweetness and my good fruit, to hold sway over the trees?’

speaker: fig-tree
name: The fig tree
text: Should I stop giving my sweetness and my good fruit, to hold sway over the trees?

speaker: jotham
text: Then the trees said to the grapevine, ‘Come and reign over us.’

speaker: trees
text: Come and reign over us.

speaker: jotham
text: But the grapevine replied, ‘Should I stop giving my wine that cheers both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’

speaker: grapevine
name: The grapevine
text: Should I stop giving my wine that cheers both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?

speaker: jotham
text: Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, ‘Come and reign over us.’

speaker: trees
text: Come and reign over us.

speaker: jotham
text: But the thornbush replied, ‘If you really are anointing me as king over you, come and find refuge in my shade. But if not, may fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.’

speaker: thornbush
name: The thornbush
text: If you really are anointing me as king over you, come and find refuge in my shade. But if not, may fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.

speaker: jotham
text: Now if you have acted faithfully and honestly in making Abimelech king, if you have done well by Jerubbaal and his family, and if you have done to him as he deserves—

speaker: jotham
text: for my father fought for you and risked his life to deliver you from the hand of Midian,

speaker: jotham
text: but you have risen up against my father’s house this day and killed his seventy sons on a single stone, and you have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the leaders of Shechem because he is your brother—

speaker: jotham
text: if you have acted faithfully and honestly toward Jerubbaal and his house this day, then may you rejoice in Abimelech, and he in you.

speaker: jotham
text: But if not, may fire come from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and may fire come from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech.

speaker: gaal
name: Gaal
text: Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is not Zebul his officer? You are to serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem. Why should we serve Abimelech?

speaker: gaal
text: If only this people were under my authority, I would remove Abimelech; I would say to him, ‘Muster your army and come out!’

speaker: gaal
text: Muster your army and come out!

speaker: zebul
name: Zebul
text: Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.

speaker: zebul
text: Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields.

speaker: zebul
text: And in the morning at sunrise, get up and advance against the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, do to them whatever you are able.

speaker: gaal
text: Look, people are coming down from the mountains!

speaker: zebul
text: The shadows of the mountains look like men to you.

speaker: gaal
text: Look, people are coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming by way of the Diviners’ Oak.

speaker: zebul
text: Where is your gloating now?

speaker: zebul
text: You said, ‘Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?’ Are these not the people you ridiculed? Go out now and fight them!

speaker: gaal
text: Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?

speaker: abimelech
text: Hurry and do what you have seen me do.

speaker: abimelech
text: Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’

speaker: israelites
name: The Israelites
text: A woman killed him.

speaker: israelites
name: The Israelites
text: We have sinned against You, for we have indeed forsaken our God and served the Baals.

speaker: god
name: The LORD
text: When the Egyptians, Amorites, Ammonites, Philistines,

speaker: god
text: Sidonians, Amalekites, and Maonites oppressed you and you cried out to Me, did I not save you from their hands?

speaker: god
text: But you have forsaken Me and served other gods, so I will no longer save you.

speaker: god
text: Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them save you in your time of trouble.

speaker: israelites
text: We have sinned,

speaker: israelites
text: Deal with us as You see fit; but please deliver us today!

speaker: rulers-of-gilead
name: The rulers of Gilead
text: Whoever will launch the attack against the Ammonites will be the head of all who live in Gilead.

speaker: brothers-of-jephthah
name: Gilead’s sons (Jephthah’s brothers)
text: You shall have no inheritance in our father’s house, because you are the son of another woman.

speaker: elders-of-gilead
name: The elders of Gilead
text: Come,

speaker: elders-of-gilead
text: be our commander, so that we can fight against the Ammonites.

speaker: jephthah
name: Jephthah
text: Did you not hate me and expel me from my father’s house? Why then have you come to me now, when you are in distress?

speaker: elders-of-gilead
text: This is why we now turn to you, that you may go with us, fight the Ammonites, and become leader over all of us who live in Gilead.

speaker: jephthah
text: If you take me back to fight the Ammonites and the LORD gives them to me, will I really be your leader?

speaker: elders-of-gilead
text: The LORD is our witness if we do not do as you say.

speaker: jephthah
text: What do you have against me that you have come to fight against my land?

speaker: king-of-the-ammonites
name: The king of the Ammonites
text: When Israel came up out of Egypt, they seized my land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and all the way to the Jordan. Now, therefore, restore it peaceably.

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
name: Jephthah’s messengers
text: This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take away the land of Moab or of the Ammonites.

speaker: jephthah
text: Israel did not take away the land of Moab or of the Ammonites.

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: But when Israel came up out of Egypt, they traveled through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.

speaker: jephthah
text: But when Israel came up out of Egypt, they traveled through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let us pass through your land,’ but the king of Edom would not listen. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he would not consent. So Israel stayed in Kadesh.

speaker: jephthah
text: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let us pass through your land,’ but the king of Edom would not listen. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he would not consent. So Israel stayed in Kadesh.

speaker: israelites
name: Israel
text: Please let us pass through your land,

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: Then Israel traveled through the wilderness and bypassed the lands of Edom and Moab. They came to the east side of the land of Moab and camped on the other side of the Arnon. But they did not enter the territory of Moab, since the Arnon was its border.

speaker: jephthah
text: Then Israel traveled through the wilderness and bypassed the lands of Edom and Moab. They came to the east side of the land of Moab and camped on the other side of the Arnon. But they did not enter the territory of Moab, since the Arnon was its border.

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, ‘Please let us pass through your land into our own place.’

speaker: jephthah
text: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, ‘Please let us pass through your land into our own place.’

speaker: israelites
text: Please let us pass through your land into our own place.

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: But Sihon would not trust Israel to pass through his territory. So he gathered all his people, encamped in Jahaz, and fought with Israel.

speaker: jephthah
text: But Sihon would not trust Israel to pass through his territory. So he gathered all his people, encamped in Jahaz, and fought with Israel.

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: Then the LORD, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, who defeated them. So Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who inhabited that country,

speaker: jephthah
text: Then the LORD, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, who defeated them. So Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who inhabited that country,

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: seizing all the land from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.

speaker: jephthah
text: seizing all the land from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: Now since the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites from before His people Israel, should you now possess it?

speaker: jephthah
text: Now since the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites from before His people Israel, should you now possess it?

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: Do you not possess whatever your god Chemosh grants you? So also, we possess whatever the LORD our God has granted us.

speaker: jephthah
text: Do you not possess whatever your god Chemosh grants you? So also, we possess whatever the LORD our God has granted us.

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: Are you now so much better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel or fight against them?

speaker: jephthah
text: Are you now so much better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel or fight against them?

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: For three hundred years Israel has lived in Heshbon, Aroer, and their villages, as well as all the cities along the banks of the Arnon. Why did you not take them back during that time?

speaker: jephthah
text: For three hundred years Israel has lived in Heshbon, Aroer, and their villages, as well as all the cities along the banks of the Arnon. Why did you not take them back during that time?

speaker: messengers-of-jephthah
text: I have not sinned against you, but you have done me wrong by waging war against me. May the LORD, the Judge, decide today between the Israelites and the Ammonites.

speaker: jephthah
text: I have not sinned against you, but you have done me wrong by waging war against me. May the LORD, the Judge, decide today between the Israelites and the Ammonites.

speaker: jephthah
text: If indeed You will deliver the Ammonites into my hand,

speaker: jephthah
text: then whatever comes out the door of my house to greet me on my triumphant return from the Ammonites will belong to the LORD, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering.

speaker: jephthah
text: No! Not my daughter! You have brought me to my knees! You have brought great misery upon me, for I have given my word to the LORD and cannot take it back.

speaker: daughter-of-jephthah
name: Jephthah’s daughter
text: My father,

speaker: daughter-of-jephthah
text: you have given your word to the LORD. Do to me as you have said, for the LORD has avenged you of your enemies, the Ammonites.

speaker: daughter-of-jephthah
text: Let me do this one thing: Let me wander for two months through the mountains with my friends and mourn my virginity.

speaker: jephthah
text: Go,

speaker: ephraimites
name: The men of Ephraim
text: Why have you crossed over to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We will burn your house down with you inside!

speaker: jephthah
name: Jephthah
text: My people and I had a serious conflict with the Ammonites, and when I called, you did not save me out of their hands.

speaker: jephthah
text: When I saw that you would not save me, I risked my life and crossed over to the Ammonites, and the LORD delivered them into my hand. Why then have you come today to fight against me?

speaker: ephraimites
text: You Gileadites are fugitives in Ephraim, living in the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh.

speaker: unnamed-fugitive-from-ephraim
name: Unnamed fugitive from Ephraim
text: Let me cross over,

speaker: gileadites
name: The Gileadites
text: Are you an Ephraimite?

speaker: unnamed-fugitive-from-ephraim
text: No,

speaker: gileadites
text: Please say Shibboleth.

speaker: unnamed-fugitive-from-ephraim
text: Sibboleth,

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
name: The angel of the LORD
text: It is true that you are barren and have no children; but you will conceive and give birth to a son.

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: Now please be careful not to drink wine or strong drink, and not to eat anything unclean.

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: For behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son. And no razor shall come over his head, because the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb, and he will begin the deliverance of Israel from the hand of the Philistines.

speaker: wife-of-manoah
name: Manoah’s wife
text: A man of God came to me. His appearance was like the angel of God, exceedingly awesome. I did not ask him where he came from, and he did not tell me his name.

speaker: wife-of-manoah
text: But he said to me, ‘Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son. Now, therefore, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean, because the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb until the day of his death.’

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son. Now, therefore, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean, because the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb until the day of his death.

speaker: manoah
name: Manoah
text: Please, O Lord, let the man of God You sent us come to us again to teach us how to raise the boy who is to be born.

speaker: wife-of-manoah
text: Behold, the man who came to me the other day has reappeared!

speaker: manoah
text: Are you the man who spoke to my wife?

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: I am,

speaker: manoah
text: When your words come to pass, what will be the boy’s rule of life and mission?

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: Your wife is to do everything I told her.

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: She must not eat anything that comes from the vine, nor drink any wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean. She must do everything I have commanded her.

speaker: manoah
text: Please stay here,

speaker: manoah
text: and we will prepare a young goat for you.

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: Even if I stay, I will not eat your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.

speaker: manoah
text: What is your name, so that we may honor you when your word comes to pass?

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: Why do you ask my name,

speaker: angel-of-the-lord
text: since it is beyond comprehension?

speaker: manoah
text: We are going to die,

speaker: manoah
text: for we have seen God!

speaker: wife-of-manoah
text: If the LORD had intended to kill us, He would not have accepted the burnt offering and the grain offering from our hands, nor would He have shown us all these things or spoken to us this way.

speaker: samson
name: Samson
text: I have seen a daughter of the Philistines in Timnah. Now get her for me as a wife.

speaker: manoah-and-wife
name: Samson’s father and mother
text: Can’t you find a young woman among your relatives or among any of our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?

speaker: samson
text: Get her for me, for she is pleasing to my eyes.

speaker: samson
text: Let me tell you a riddle,

speaker: samson
text: If you can solve it for me within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.

speaker: samson
text: But if you cannot solve it, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.

speaker: thirty-philistine-companions
name: Thirty Philistine companions
text: Tell us your riddle,

speaker: thirty-philistine-companions
text: Let us hear it.

speaker: samson
text: Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.

speaker: thirty-philistine-companions
text: Entice your husband to explain the riddle to us, or we will burn you and your father’s household to death. Did you invite us here to rob us?

speaker: wife-of-samson
name: Samson’s wife
text: You hate me! You do not really love me! You have posed to my people a riddle, but have not explained it to me.

speaker: samson
text: Look,

speaker: samson
text: I have not even explained it to my father or mother, so why should I explain it to you?

speaker: thirty-philistine-companions
text: What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?

speaker: samson
text: If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have solved my riddle!

speaker: samson
name: Samson
text: I want to go to my wife in her room,

speaker: father-in-law-of-samson
name: Samson’s wife’s father (the Timnite)
text: I was sure that you thoroughly hated her,

speaker: father-in-law-of-samson
text: so I gave her to one of the men who accompanied you. Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please take her instead.

speaker: samson
text: This time I will be blameless in doing harm to the Philistines.

speaker: philistines
name: The Philistines
text: Who did this?

speaker: unnamed-informants
name: Unnamed informants
text: It was Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite,

speaker: unnamed-informants
text: For his wife was given to his companion.

speaker: samson
text: Because you have done this, I will not rest until I have taken vengeance upon you.

speaker: men-of-judah
name: The men of Judah
text: Why have you attacked us?

speaker: philistines
text: We have come to arrest Samson and pay him back for what he has done to us.

speaker: men-of-judah
text: Do you not realize that the Philistines rule over us? What have you done to us?

speaker: samson
text: I have done to them what they did to me,

speaker: men-of-judah
text: We have come down to arrest you and hand you over to the Philistines.

speaker: samson
text: Swear to me that you will not kill me yourselves.

speaker: men-of-judah
text: No,

speaker: men-of-judah
text: we will not kill you, but we will tie you up securely and hand you over to them.

speaker: samson
text: With the jawbone of a donkey I have piled them into heaps. With the jawbone of a donkey I have slain a thousand men.

speaker: samson
text: You have accomplished this great deliverance through Your servant. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?

speaker: gazites
name: The Gazites
text: Let us wait until dawn; then we will kill him.

speaker: lords-of-the-philistines
name: The lords of the Philistines
text: Entice him and find out the source of his great strength and how we can overpower him to tie him up and subdue him. Then each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.

speaker: delilah
name: Delilah
text: Please tell me the source of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued.

speaker: samson
name: Samson
text: If they tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I will become as weak as any other man.

speaker: delilah
text: Samson, the Philistines are here!

speaker: delilah
text: You have mocked me and lied to me! Now please tell me how you can be tied up.

speaker: samson
text: If they tie me up with new ropes that have never been used, I will become as weak as any other man.

speaker: delilah
text: Samson, the Philistines are here!

speaker: delilah
text: You have mocked me and lied to me all along! Tell me how you can be tied up.

speaker: samson
text: If you weave the seven braids of my head into the web of a loom and tighten it with a pin, I will become as weak as any other man.

speaker: delilah
text: Samson, the Philistines are here!

speaker: delilah
text: How can you say, ‘I love you,’

speaker: samson
text: I love you,

speaker: delilah
text: when your heart is not with me? This is the third time you have mocked me and failed to reveal to me the source of your great strength!

speaker: samson
text: My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb. If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, and I will become as weak as any other man.

speaker: delilah
text: Come up once more, for he has revealed to me all that is in his heart.

speaker: delilah
text: Samson, the Philistines are here!

speaker: samson
text: I will escape as I did before and shake myself free.

speaker: lords-of-the-philistines
text: Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hands.

speaker: philistines
name: The Philistine people
text: Our god has delivered into our hands our enemy who destroyed our land and multiplied our dead.

speaker: philistines
text: Call for Samson to entertain us.

speaker: samson
text: Lead me where I can feel the pillars supporting the temple, so I can lean against them.

speaker: samson
text: O Lord GOD, please remember me. Strengthen me, O God, just once more, so that with one vengeful blow I may pay back the Philistines for my two eyes.

speaker: samson
text: Let me die with the Philistines.

speaker: micah
name: Micah
text: The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you and about which I heard you utter a curse—I have the silver here with me; I took it.

speaker: mother-of-micah
name: Micah’s mother
text: Blessed be my son by the LORD!

speaker: mother-of-micah
text: I wholly dedicate the silver to the LORD for my son’s benefit, to make a graven image and a molten idol. Therefore I will now return it to you.

speaker: micah
text: Where are you from?

speaker: jonathan-the-levite
name: Jonathan (the young Levite)
text: I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,

speaker: jonathan-the-levite
text: and I am on my way to settle wherever I can find a place.

speaker: micah
text: Stay with me,

speaker: micah
text: and be my father and priest, and I will give you ten shekels of silver per year, a suit of clothes, and your provisions.

speaker: micah
text: Now I know that the LORD will be good to me, because a Levite has become my priest.

speaker: danites
name: The Danites
text: Go and explore the land,

speaker: five-danite-spies
name: The five Danite spies
text: Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?

speaker: jonathan-the-levite
name: Jonathan (the young Levite)
text: Micah has done this and that for me,

speaker: jonathan-the-levite
text: and he has hired me to be his priest.

speaker: five-danite-spies
text: Please inquire of God to determine whether we will have a successful journey.

speaker: jonathan-the-levite
text: Go in peace. The LORD is watching over your journey.

speaker: danites
text: What did you find?

speaker: five-danite-spies
text: Come on, let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and it is very good. Why would you fail to act? Do not hesitate to go there and take possession of the land!

speaker: five-danite-spies
text: When you enter, you will come to an unsuspecting people and a spacious land, for God has delivered it into your hand. It is a place where nothing on earth is lacking.

speaker: five-danite-spies
text: Did you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household gods, a graven image, and a molten idol? Now think about what you should do.
tag: the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish

speaker: jonathan-the-levite
text: What are you doing?

speaker: five-danite-spies
text: Be quiet,

speaker: five-danite-spies
text: Put your hand over your mouth and come with us and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one person or a priest for a tribe and family in Israel?

speaker: danites
text: What is the matter with you that you have called out such a company?

speaker: micah
name: Micah
text: You took the gods I had made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have? How can you say to me, ‘What is the matter with you?’

speaker: danites
text: What is the matter with you?

speaker: danites
text: Do not raise your voice against us, or angry men will attack you, and you and your family will lose your lives.

speaker: father-of-the-concubine
name: The girl’s father
text: Refresh your heart with a morsel of bread, and then you can go.

speaker: father-of-the-concubine
text: Please agree to stay overnight and let your heart be merry.

speaker: father-of-the-concubine
text: Please refresh your heart.

speaker: father-of-the-concubine
text: Look, the day is drawing to a close. Please spend the night. See, the day is almost over. Spend the night here, that your heart may be merry. Then you can get up early tomorrow for your journey home.

speaker: unnamed-servant-of-levite
name: The Levite’s servant
text: Please, let us stop at this Jebusite city and spend the night here.

speaker: unnamed-levite-of-ephraim
name: Unnamed Levite of Ephraim
text: We will not turn aside to the city of foreigners, where there are no Israelites. We will go on to Gibeah.

speaker: unnamed-levite-of-ephraim
text: Come, let us try to reach one of these towns to spend the night in Gibeah or Ramah.

speaker: unnamed-old-man-in-gibeah
name: Unnamed old man in Gibeah
text: Where are you going, and where have you come from?

speaker: unnamed-levite-of-ephraim
text: We are traveling from Bethlehem in Judah to the remote hill country of Ephraim, where I am from. I went to Bethlehem in Judah, and now I am going to the house of the LORD; but no one has taken me into his home,

speaker: unnamed-levite-of-ephraim
text: even though there is both straw and feed for our donkeys, and bread and wine for me and the maidservant and young man with me. There is nothing that we, your servants, lack.

speaker: unnamed-old-man-in-gibeah
text: Peace to you,

speaker: unnamed-old-man-in-gibeah
text: Let me supply everything you need. Only do not spend the night in the square.

speaker: wicked-men-of-gibeah
name: The wicked men of Gibeah
text: Bring out the man who came to your house, so we can have relations with him!

speaker: unnamed-old-man-in-gibeah
text: No, my brothers, do not do this wicked thing! After all, this man is a guest in my house. Do not commit this outrage.

speaker: unnamed-old-man-in-gibeah
text: Look, let me bring out my virgin daughter and the man’s concubine, and you can use them and do with them as you wish. But do not do such a vile thing to this man.

speaker: unnamed-levite-of-ephraim
text: Get up,

speaker: unnamed-levite-of-ephraim
text: Let us go.

speaker: israelites
name: The Israelites
text: Nothing like this has been seen or done from the day the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt until this day. Think it over, take counsel, and speak up!

speaker: israelites
name: The Israelites
text: Tell us, how did this wicked thing happen?

speaker: unnamed-levite-of-ephraim
name: Unnamed Levite of Ephraim
text: I and my concubine came to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
tag: the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman,

speaker: unnamed-levite-of-ephraim
text: And during the night, the men of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house. They intended to kill me, but they abused my concubine, and she died.

speaker: unnamed-levite-of-ephraim
text: Then I took my concubine, cut her into pieces, and sent her throughout the land of Israel’s inheritance, because they had committed a lewd and disgraceful act in Israel.

speaker: unnamed-levite-of-ephraim
text: Behold, all you Israelites, give your advice and verdict here and now.

speaker: israelites
text: Not one of us will return to his tent or to his house.

speaker: israelites
text: Now this is what we will do to Gibeah: We will go against it as the lot dictates.

speaker: israelites
text: We will take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to supply provisions for the army when they go to Gibeah in Benjamin to punish them for the atrocity they have committed in Israel.

speaker: israelites
text: What is this wickedness that has occurred among you?

speaker: israelites
text: Hand over the wicked men of Gibeah so we can put them to death and purge Israel of this evil.

speaker: israelites
text: Who of us shall go up first to fight against the Benjamites?

speaker: god
name: The LORD
text: Judah will be first,

speaker: israelites
text: Should we again draw near for battle against our brothers the Benjamites?

speaker: god
text: Go up against them.

speaker: israelites
text: Should we again go out to battle against our brothers the Benjamites, or should we stop?

speaker: god
text: Fight, for tomorrow I will deliver them into your hand.

speaker: benjamites
name: The Benjamites
text: We are defeating them as before,

speaker: israelites
text: Let us retreat and draw them away from the city onto the roads.

speaker: benjamites
text: They are defeated before us as in the first battle.

speaker: israelites
name: The Israelites
text: Not one of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjamite.

speaker: israelites
text: Why, O LORD God of Israel,

speaker: israelites
text: has this happened in Israel? Today in Israel one tribe is missing!

speaker: israelites
text: Who among all the tribes of Israel did not come to the assembly before the LORD?

speaker: israelites
text: Today a tribe is cut off from Israel.

speaker: israelites
text: What should we do about wives for the survivors, since we have sworn by the LORD not to give them our daughters in marriage?

speaker: israelites
text: Which one of the tribes of Israel failed to come up before the LORD at Mizpah?

speaker: israelites
text: Go and put to the sword those living in Jabesh-gilead, including women and children.

speaker: israelites
text: This is what you are to do: Devote to destruction every male, as well as every female who has had relations with a man.

speaker: elders-of-the-congregation
name: The elders of the congregation
text: What should we do about wives for those who remain, since the women of Benjamin have been destroyed?

speaker: elders-of-the-congregation
text: There must be heirs for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe of Israel will not be wiped out.

speaker: elders-of-the-congregation
text: But we cannot give them our daughters as wives.

speaker: israelites
text: Cursed is he who gives a wife to a Benjamite.

speaker: elders-of-the-congregation
text: But look,

speaker: elders-of-the-congregation
text: there is a yearly feast to the LORD in Shiloh, which is north of Bethel east of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.

speaker: elders-of-the-congregation
text: Go, hide in the vineyards

speaker: elders-of-the-congregation
text: and watch. When you see the daughters of Shiloh come out to perform their dances, each of you is to come out of the vineyards, catch for himself a wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

speaker: elders-of-the-congregation
text: When their fathers or brothers come to us to complain, we will tell them, ‘Do us a favor by helping them, since we did not get wives for each of them in the war. Since you did not actually give them your daughters, you have no guilt.’

speaker: elders-of-the-congregation
text: Do us a favor by helping them, since we did not get wives for each of them in the war. Since you did not actually give them your daughters, you have no guilt.
